mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous year same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls versus prior year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle that boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 3% and UNRATE > 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS YoY growth > 5%) alongside a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 YoY growth < 0%) signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS YoY > 5% and GDPC1 YoY < 0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its previous peak for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth offsets cost pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous peak for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during three consecutive months when PAYEMS exceed prior peak.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 500K units for six consecutive months signals a deepening housing slump, which reduces construction-related economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during six consecutive months when HOUST < 500K.
